# Paper Example Files Description 📄

The example files in this directory are sourced from an academic paper on **arXiv**:
- Neural Controlled Differential Equations for Irregular Time Series
- Paper URL: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2005.08926v2

## File List 📋

These are complete [LaTeX source files](https://arxiv.org/src/2005.08926v2) for automatic processing by the Python project:

* **`main.tex`**: The main document of the paper, containing the full content and structure.
* **`main.bbl`**: The bibliography list file generated by BibTeX.
* **`main.bib`**: The BibTeX bibliography database storing all referenced entries.
* **`custom.sty`**: A custom LaTeX package file for defining special formats and commands.

## Runtime Environment Requirements ⚙️

Before running the Python project, ensure your system meets one of the following conditions:

1. **Recommended Configuration: LaTeX Environment**
   * The project will automatically invoke LaTeX to compile `.tex` files.
   * Please install a LaTeX distribution first, such as TeX Live or MikTeX.
   * **Download Links**:
     * TeX Live: [https://www.tug.org/texlive/](https://www.tug.org/texlive/)
     * MikTeX: [https://miktex.org/](https://miktex.org/)

2. **Alternative Option: LibreOffice**
   * The project can use LibreOffice to convert PDF to Word.
   * **Download Link**: [https://www.libreoffice.org/](https://www.libreoffice.org/)

## Usage Instructions 🚀

1. **Configure YAML**: Open `config.yaml` and set `data_path` to point to this directory.
2. **Run the Project**: Execute `python -m trans`. The program will:
   * Prioritize using LaTeX to compile and generate a PDF.
   * Then attempt to convert the PDF to Word using LibreOffice.
   * If the above fails, automatically invoke the `pdf2docx` library for conversion.
3. **Manual Conversion**: If automatic conversion fails, you can manually convert the generated PDF to Word.

## Citation Note 📝

If you refer to this paper in your research, please cite the original source mentioned above.
